Guardian politics live (Andrew Sparrow) — first published Thursday 24 September 2026 08:59 BST, last updated 17:31 BST. Council tax post filed ~15:30 BST.

HEADLINE: Resolution Foundation says the structure of council tax hands Londoners the equivalent of a £3bn-a-year property tax subsidy, with households outside the capital paying hundreds of pounds a year more than under a fair system. Report: "Home Economics", https://www.resolutionfoundation.org/app/uploads/2026/09/home-economics.pdf

FACTS (Guardian, quoting the Resolution Foundation report):
- "London paid £3.1bn too little in residential property tax in 2024-25, with every other region besides the south-east and east of England overpaying. If the rest of England had paid taxes as a proportion of the value of their homes at a rate as low as that in London, regions outside of London would have paid £12.3bn less in tax."
- "By 2030-31, and compared to an alternative of property being taxed at a uniform rate everywhere, 61% of households would be overpaying tax by an average of £430 a year, and 36% of households would be underpaying by an average of £680 a year."
- Council tax bands are still based on 1991 property values. When council tax was set up, a top-band property was worth at least eight times a bottom-band one but paid at most three times the bill.
- "Now, a property at the bottom of the top band in Richmond-upon-Thames has a price 15 times larger than one at the top of the bottom band in Hull, while their council tax bill is only just over double. Alternatively: the resident of Hull is paying over £1,800 more each year than if they faced the same effective tax rate as the resident of Richmond-upon-Thames."
- The report calls for council tax to be replaced with "a proportional tax charged at 0.7% of property value" and for stamp duty to be abolished, both phased in gradually.
- The combined property tax burden as a share of house value is highest in the north of England and lowest in London.

QUOTE:
Hannah Aldridge, senior research and policy analyst, Resolution Foundation (Guardian): "The UK raises more tax revenue from the homes we live in than most other advanced economies. Unfortunately, our two main housing taxes – council tax and stamp duty – are terribly designed, grossly unfair and economically harmful." / "The economic and fairness case for overhauling our housing taxes are clear. But the politics of reform has got hung up on those who lose out – such as those living in gentrified areas of London – even though most households in England would pay less tax." / "Housing taxes cannot be fixed overnight. But the chancellor should set out a sensible roadmap to reform in the budget next month."

HOUSEHOLD ANGLE: strong. Council tax bills, stamp duty, and a direct call on Chancellor John Healey ahead of next month's Budget.
